notes: §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR6: "After execution of the USE procedure, control is transferred to the invoking routine in the input-output control system. If the I-O status value does not indicate a critical input-output error, the input-output control system returns control to the next executable statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception. If the I-O status value does indicate a critical error, the implementor determines what action is taken." Every I-O statement emits EmitUseHook after its status store; at 85 no EC-I-O checking or RESUME exists (>>TURN and RESUME are refused, COBOL0900 and COBOL0876, probed), so the hook is EmitPlainIoCheck's call of the __IoCheck that EmitUseMachinery emits. That function runs the selected section as a bounded call (RunUseCall into the void __RunUse of EmitRunUseBody, the section's first paragraph to its last), returns when the section's last statement has run, and the generated code then falls to the text after the hook: the statement's own phrase tests, none of which holds for a status the hook handled, and then the next statement. For a critical status (§1985:VII.1.3.5: "any that begin with the digit 3 or 4, and any that begin with the digit 9 that the implementor defines as critical") the implementor's action is the same return: EmitUseHook emits the run unit's termination (EmitUncoveredFatalTermination, CobolFile.TerminateOnUncoveredFatalStatus) only for a file with no FILE STATUS clause when no USE procedure ran, so after a USE procedure execution always continues (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-103, which cites the 2023 clauses only). No edition arm. The witness returns from a two-paragraph USE procedure to the statement after a READ inside an IF, and to the end of a PERFORMed paragraph whose last statement is the READ. Probed further at --std 85, files without a FILE STATUS clause: after the USE procedure (which PERFORMs a paragraph of its section and leaves by GO TO to its last paragraph) the statement after the I-O statement runs for OPEN (35, 41), READ (47), CLOSE (42), WRITE (48) and REWRITE (49, 43), under a file-name USE and under USE ... ON I-O and ON OUTPUT; a failing READ with both AT END and NOT AT END runs neither phrase after the procedure; inside an inline PERFORM 2 TIMES the loop goes on with the statement after the READ.

next.reason: Non-critical return is kept: 1985 'returns control to the next executable statement following the input-output statement'; §2023:14.9.49.4 GR7 b) 'control is returned to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the input-output statement'. The critical case changes: 1985 'If the I-O status value does indicate a critical error, the implementor determines what action is taken' (unconstrained, §1985:VII.1.3.5). §2023:14.9.49.4 GR7 c) 'the implementor determines what action is taken as described in 9.1.13', and §2023:9.1.13.1 constrains it: 'The implementor may either continue or terminate the execution of the run unit. If the implementor chooses to continue ..., control is transferred to the end of the statement ... Any NOT AT END or NOT INVALID KEY phrase specified for that statement is ignored'; §2023:14.6.13.1.3 GR3 then applies the fatal-exception rules. Implementor latitude narrowed (fatal class adds 7x, line-sequential only).
